items.trecho: A Embraer é uma das líderes mundiais da indústria aeroespacial, atuando nos segmentos de Aviação Comercial, Jatos Executivos, Defesa & Segurança e Serviços & Suporte.

With more than five decades of expertise in designing, manufacturing, certifying and supporting high performance aircraft in commercial aviation, business aviation and defense, Embraer became a global reference in the aeronautical industry.

A Embraer tornou-se a terceira maior fabricante de jatos comerciais do mundo e líder absoluta no segmento de até 130 assentos. Para atender demandas globais estabeleceu unidades industriais, escritórios e centros de distribuição de peças e serviços na América, África, Ásia e Europa.

In 2000, Embraer became a public limited company (Sociedade Anônima) with its shares traded in both the United States (NYSE) and Brazil (B3). Embraer has divisions for commercial, executive, military, and agricultural aviation; it also maintains an incubator for aerospace technologies and businesses

It initially focused on supplying military aircraft to the , but by the 1980s began producing a series of successful commuter and regional airliners for export. The company was privatized in 1994 and began expanding to the production of larger regional airliners and smaller . secoes.texto:
In the mid-1990s, the company pursued a product line focused on small commercial airplanes over the military aircraft that had previously made up the majority of its manufacturing. It soon expanded to the production of larger regional airliners in the 70–110 seat range, and smaller . 8 [ ] business jets 17 [ ]
By May 2019, Embraer considered developing a of turboprop in the 50–70 seat range, complementing the , so as to free engineering resources. It would compete against older and designs for 1.5 to 2h flights over . In August 2021, Embraer released a new configuration with quieter aft-mounted engines for a 70-90 seat aircraft, with the E-Jet cross-section, aiming for a 2022 launch and a 2027/2028 service entry. new family regional airliners E-Jet E2 22 [ ] 23 [ ] ATR Dash 8 500–700 nmi (930–1,300 km) 24 [ ] 25 [ ]
In March 2026, Embraer launched the first for the , result of technology transfer agreements signed between the Brazilian and Swedish governments in 2014, for the co-production and development of the fighter. JAS F-39 Gripen Brazilian Air Force 26 [ ] 27 [ ]
At the 2000 , Embraer introduced the , a variant of the , which entered service in 2002. was created as a dedicated subsidiary in 2005. That same year, the was envisioned as an similar to the , competing with and . It was introduced in 2008 and is the basis of the larger . The midsize and were jointly developed as clean sheet designs, while the is a VIP version of the . In 2016, Embraer delivered its 1,000th executive jet and had a market share of 17% by volume, though it lacked an ultra-long-range large cabin jet. In October 2018 Embraer announced two new business jets—the in the midsize cabin category—and the in the super midsize category. Farnborough Airshow Legacy 600 business jet Embraer Regional Jet 28 [ ] Embraer Executive Jets Phenom 100 air taxi Eclipse 500 Cessna Hawker Beechcraft Phenom 300 Legacy 450 Legacy 500 Lineage 1000 E190 29 [ ] Praetor 500 Praetor 600 30 [ ]
As of 2026, Embraer remains dominant in the market for small and medium-sized private jets, with the Phenom 300 remaining the best seller in its class for the 14th year. 31 [ ]
On April 19, 2007, Embraer announced it was considering the production of a twin-jet military transport. Work began in May 2009 with funding from the Brazilian Air Force. Correios, the Brazilian postal service, has shown interest in buying this aircraft. Using much of the technology developed for the Embraer 190, the C-390 would carry up to 23 tons of cargo and aims to replace Cold War-era cargo aircraft.
As a result, Embraer developed the C-390 Millennium, a medium-size, twin-engine, jet-powered military transport aircraft with multi-role capability adapted to various missions. Brazil has been operating 6 units since 2019. Initially, thirty aircraft (including two prototypes) were to be delivered to the Brazilian Air Force. In February 2022, a new agreement was reached to supply 22 aircraft, with deliveries scheduled until 2034. 32 [ ] 33 [ ] 34 [ ]

Brazil and Canada engaged in an international, adjudicated trade dispute over government subsidies to domestic plane-makers in the late 1990s and early 2000s. The determined that both countries had provided illegal subsidies to what were supposed to be privately owned industries. Brazil ran an illegal subsidy program, Proex, benefiting its national aviation industry from at least 1999–2000, and Canada illegally subsidized its indigenous regional airliner industry including in export contracts, comprising . Much of the growth is led by the E2 line, due to increased travel on regional, short distance routes, as well as its relatively fast delivery time of less than two years. [ edit ] Latest comment: 5 months ago 5 comments 3 people in discussion @: Back in October 2021 you made removing the 'E' prefix from the entire E-jet range (E170 to E195). Has there been any discussion about this naming policy, either here or elsewhere? Do you still believe it to be correct? RickyCourtney this edit Just a heads-up, I am going to disagree, and I will bring plenty of examples, not least of which are the number of sources all talking about Finnair recently ordering up to 46 aircraft. One of those sources is Embraer's own Media Center! Other sources include United, KLM, Luxair, aviationinfo.org, skybrary.aero, simpleflying.com, and Embraer E195-E2 Aviation Week (not a perfect example, I should have used American Airlines, meh!) Embraer Media Center, March 23, 2026 - Finnair selects Embraer E195-E2 Embraer Press Release, February 28, 2018 - granted certification by ANAC, FAA and EASA Embraer E190-E2 Aviation Week - Marathon Airlines Adds Fourth Embraer E195 Aviation Week - South Africa's Airlink Expands Reach With New Fleet Embraer E195-E2 Aviation Week - Air Serbia Completes Fleet Modernization With Final Delivery Embraer E195-E1 United Airlines Embraer E-175 () WendlingCrusader talk 02:38, 6 April 2026 (UTC) Reply First off, I welcome this conversation and I want to make it clear that I’m open minded, I’m not dead set either way, but some consistency would be nice. Secondly, I think it’s going to be hard to establish a definitive common name because Embraer’s communications has been all over the place. I based my initial changes based on a few official Embraer sources: Airport Planning Manual Audited Financial Prospectus Q425 Backlog and Deliveries I would consider these sources more authoritative than the marketing materials, as the Airport Planning Manual is a long-standing official document, and financial statements are audited and tend to have more internal review, with more "eyes" checking every line. Pinging those involved prior discussions: , () User:Canterbury Tail User:Dfadden RickyCourtney talk 02:53, 6 April 2026 (UTC) Reply Thanks for the ping. As i mentioned previously, I consider financial reports and airport planning manuals pretty niche, except within the industry. But more importantly, these are primary sources published by Embraer. tells us that primary sources should be treated with care, supported by reliable secondary sources and not given undue weight. So my interpretation of policy is that those sources, at least in a wikipedia context are authoritative than secondary sources, including the articles mentioned above by @ from publications like Aviation Week. (I'd caution against Simple Flying sources though, there has been some debate on wikipedia about that particular outlet's reliability). () WP:PSTS less WendlingCrusader Dfadden talk 01:58, 8 April 2026 (UTC) Reply Returning to @'s list of sources; note that these are not pure English-language sources; they are in-house translations of Embraer's original Portuguese documents? For instance the Q425 Backlog and Deliveries PDF is marked "ri.embraer.com.br/en" RickyCourtney This is the Portuguese version; original CARTEIRA DE PEDIDOS & ENTREGAS 4T25 Maybe I am nit-picking, but just supposing Embraer had translated it in-house, how would we approach these documents? ? not WP:NONENG Yes, of course I accept that Embraer's preferred presentation is unlikely to change through translation; but could it be another nail in the coffin? Probably not... which sources do we prefer FWIW I am raising a similar issue regarding Czech manufacturer LET, who appear to have dropped the hyphen from , specifically in literature that is derived The Czech alphabet is full of and other diacritics, and they do not use Q, W and X. Maybe they don't use hyphens either? But English language media does, and invariably names the aircraft type as "L-410", regardless of LET's own preference. Sorry - I'm digressing! Let L-410 Turbolet from their own language. háčeks () WendlingCrusader talk 13:21, 11 April 2026 (UTC) Reply A full month has elapsed, which is time enough for any further input. To add to the comments above, I will note that there seems to be no problem with the & associated family (EMB 120, etc) where it is perfectly clear that "EMB" stands for Embraer. Likewise the Embraer is never identified as just the "" (except as a redirect here on Wikipedia!) Embraer EMB 110 Bandeirante Embraer EMB 312 Tucano Embraer 312 Hence I will now revert back to the designations in place up until October 2021, as described above. result.texto: Em construção na TKMS Estaleiro Brasil Sul, o Programa Fragatas Classe Tamandaré marca uma abordagem inédita na indústria naval sul-americana com um processo totalmente digital, conhecido como "Paperless". Essa metodologia elimina o uso de documentos impressos, como desenhos e manuais técnicos, substituindo-os por soluções digitais acessíveis em dezenas de totens e tablets distribuídos pela área de produção. Os engenheiros da TKMS no Brasil e na Alemanha atualizam documentos em tempo real, assegurando maior controle, precisão e segurança das informações.A digitalização dos processos não só aumenta a segurança dos dados – um requisito essencial em projetos militares de alta confidencialidade – mas também reduz o impacto ambiental, economizando recursos que seriam utilizados para impressão e distribuição de papéis. Por meio de dispositivos conectados, os trabalhadores têm acesso imediato aos desenhos técnicos em 2D e 3D, check-lists, manuais e procedimentos operacionais atualizados em tempo real, o que otimiza etapas como apontamento de mão de obra, rastreabilidade de materiais e verificação de qualidade.Além disso, a realidade aumentada já está sendo utilizada na construção das fragatas. Com óculos especiais, os técnicos conseguem visualizar hologramas sobrepostos às peças físicas, permitindo validar o posicionamento de montagem, conferir interferências entre setores e realizar verificações de qualidade. Essa tecnologia permite também que especialistas na Alemanha ofereçam suporte remoto, orientando as equipes em tempo real.
